newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares tumble, following A shares.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares tumble, following A shares.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign B share index plunged on Thursday, following steep falls on the domestic A share market triggered by rumours of more Beijing plans to rein in the markets, brokers said.
The B share index dived 8.74 points or 6.04 percent to 135.97 on turnover of HK$53 million against HK$106 million last Friday.
There was no trading in the city's B shares from Monday to Wednesday to mark the Chinese takeover of Hong Kong.
The A share index plummeted 22.85 points or 5.30 percent to 408.27 after losing 4.07 percent on Wednesday. Turnover shrank to 6.6 billion yuan from Wednesday's 7.8 billion yuan.
"Institutions are pulling funds out of the market on the expectation of imminent new measures from Beijing to eliminate stock speculation," Cheng Li, an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The recent faster pace of new share listings, absorbing large amounts of liquidity from the markets, also exacerbated the retreat, brokers said.
"The pace of fresh money inflow is not able to keep pace with that of new listings due to the absence of the large institutions from the market," Cheng said.

Beijing recently banned state banks and enterprises and listed companies from speculative stock trading. It has also suspended some of the nation's top brokerages from trading on their own account as a penalty for trading misconduct.
The conclusion of the Hong Kong handover, which has long been a major support for sentiment, also capped buying interest, brokers said.
"More investors pulled out and moved to the sidelines after the handover euphoria failed to produce a miracle in yesterday's A share market," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"Further profit-taking in a number of over-priced shares previously driven up by speculative demand is going to put further downward pressure on the indices," Cheng said.
Brokers said the day's sharp drops made investors a bit pessimistic, but slight bargain-hunting may give the markets some support on Friday.
In the A share market, market barometer Shenzhen Development Bank dropped 1.33 yuan to 34.80 yuan on heavy volume of 14 million shares after hitting a low of 34.55 yuan.
In the B share market, floppy disk maker Shenzhen Benelux was the weakest performer with a loss of HK$0.34 to its 10 percent limit-down at HK$3.06.
Colour television maker Shenzhen Huafa Electronics, the day's sole B share gainer, edged up HK$0.05 to HK$3.80. But volume was a thin 57,700 shares.
